concept.body:
A good brief makes the result **checkable**, not automatically right. Four building blocks:

1. **Context:** What happened, who is the text for?
2. **Task:** What exactly should come out?
3. **Format:** length, structure, tone.
4. **Limits:** only these facts, mark gaps in [square brackets], no commitments.

The limits matter most. A model fills gaps with plausible text, such as an invented cause, a deadline or a discount. Marked gaps show you at once what you still need to clarify.

Measure the benefit on your own cases: how long did the draft take, how many corrections did it need? Do not adopt a time-saving figure that does not come from such measurements.
concept.takeaway: Limits in the brief make errors visible. They do not guarantee a correct result.

exercise.title: Same complaint, two briefs
exercise.instructions: Run both briefs and judge the outputs against the five criteria. Without a live model you see recorded example outputs.

props.task: Goal: a reply to the complaint that you could send after a short check.

input.label: Complaint (made up)
input.text:
Our order of twelve hydraulic pumps arrived eight working days late. We expect an explanation and reliable countermeasures.

Known so far: the cause has not been clarified internally. Only sales can approve discounts.

variants.label: Weak brief
variants.prompt: Write a reply to this customer e-mail.
variants.recorded:
Dear Ms Sommerfeld,

Thank you for your message. The delay was caused by a bottleneck at our supplier, which has since been resolved. As an apology you will receive a 10% discount on your next order. Future deliveries are guaranteed to arrive on time.

Kind regards

variants.label: Structured brief
variants.prompt:
Context: A regular customer complains about a delivery that arrived eight working days late.
Task: Draft a factual, respectful reply.
Format: e-mail, at most 120 words, with greeting and sign-off.
Limits: Use only the facts given. Do not invent a cause, deadline, compensation or measure. Mark missing details in [square brackets]. No commitments.
variants.recorded:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your feedback. Your order of twelve hydraulic pumps arrived eight working days later than agreed. We regret this.

We are clarifying the cause: [cause after internal review]. By [date] you will receive our explanation and the measures against future delays: [measures after approval].

Kind regards
[Name, role]

checks.prompt: The draft from the weak brief promises a 10% discount. Where does the figure come from?

options.text: The model filled a gap with plausible text. Nothing backs the figure.

options.feedback: No policy was in the brief. The model did not know one.

checks.explanation: Without limits a model fills gaps with plausible-sounding details. A commitment nobody approved can still create expectations and claims once it is sent.

checks.prompt: Which building block makes invented details easiest to find?

options.text: A polite greeting in the brief.
options.feedback: Politeness does not change whether gaps are marked or filled in.

options.text: The instruction to mark missing details in square brackets.
A brief that is as long as possible.
options.feedback: Length alone does not help. Limits and format do.

checks.explanation: Marked gaps show what you need to clarify instead of filling them with plausible details. You still have to check the draft.

lessons.title: Decision or remark
lessons.subtitle: What may go into AI meeting notes

concept.body:
AI meeting summaries sound finished. The risky parts are exactly the ones that create work later: **owners, deadlines and decisions nobody made.** "We could look into that" is not a decision.

When you review, sort every statement:

- **Backed:** a decision or fact that is in the notes as stated.
- **Task:** with a named person and deadline.
- **Open:** a proposal or need without a person or deadline.
- **Invented:** in none of the notes, so delete it.

Before any recording or transcription, purpose, information of participants and legal basis must be settled. In Germany, a works council has a say on technical systems that can monitor behaviour or performance (Works Constitution Act, BetrVG § 87(1) no. 6).
concept.takeaway: Every person, deadline and decision in the minutes needs a source line in the notes.

exercise.title: Check an AI summary
exercise.instructions: Compare each sentence of the summary with the notes and put it on the matching pile.

context.label: Notes from the sales meeting (made up)
context.text:
- Open pipeline EUR 1.2 million, of which EUR 400k prioritised (decided)
- Predictive maintenance pilot requested, EUR 35k; quote by 15 April (Jana)
- CRM data partly outdated, clean-up proposed
- Technical data sheet needed for plant 2

items.text: EUR 400k of the pipeline is prioritised.
items.why: In the notes as stated and marked as decided.
A fact from the notes, not a decision, but backed.

items.text: Jana sends the quote for the maintenance pilot by 15 April.
items.why: Person and deadline are in the notes.
Only a proposal, without person or deadline.

items.text: A technical data sheet is needed for plant 2.
items.why: A need without person or deadline: leave open and clarify.

items.text: The CRM clean-up has been decided and starts in May.
items.why: Only proposed in the notes. Decision and start month are invented.

items.text: Tom prepares the data sheet for plant 2 by Friday.
items.why: Neither Tom nor Friday appear in the notes.

items.text: The EUR 35k maintenance pilot is approved.

checks.prompt: The summary says: "Tom prepares the data sheet by Friday." The notes only say a data sheet is needed. What do you do?

options.text: Keep it, Tom usually does that.
options.feedback: Then the minutes record an agreement that was never made.

options.text: Delete person and deadline and mark the item as open.
Keep the sentence and tell Tom by e-mail.
options.feedback: The meeting decides responsibility, not the minutes.

checks.explanation: What is not in the notes or recording is invented. An open item is more honest than a wrong owner.

checks.prompt: You want to transcribe meetings automatically from now on. What must be settled first?

options.text: Only whether the licence includes the feature.
options.feedback: The licence only says the feature is available, not whether the processing is allowed.

options.text: Purpose, information of participants, legal basis and, where one exists, works council co-determination.
Nothing, as long as transcripts stay internal.
options.feedback: Internal transcripts also process personal data.

checks.explanation: Recording and transcription process personal data and can make behaviour or performance visible. Data protection and, where one exists, the works council therefore come first.
